html:
The World Wide Web is the system of linked pages that runs on the internet, proposed by the English computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee at CERN, the physics laboratory near Geneva, in 1989. He wanted a simple way for scientists to share documents across different computers.

The Web and the internet are not the same thing. The internet, built from the 1960s to the 1980s, is the network that connects computers. The Web is one service on top of it, built from three ideas:

  • HTML, a simple language for writing pages with links in them.
  • HTTP, the rules by which a browser asks a server for a page.
  • URLs, addresses that give every page its own name.

Berners-Lee wrote the first web server and browser in 1990, and the Web opened to the public in 1991. In 1993 CERN made the software free for anyone to use, without patents or fees, and the same year the Mosaic browser made the Web easy to use with pictures and a mouse. Growth was explosive.

Within a decade the Web had changed shopping, news, banking and mail, and it gave rise to companies such as Alibaba. It is one of the main channels of globalisation in the late twentieth century. Berners-Lee founded the World Wide Web Consortium in 1994 to keep its standards open.
